items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: Interviewer asks if the group could play 'some Sinatra' and interviewee confirms they learned 'tunes of the day, Broadway tunes, standards'

ctx.x: It would be in the latter 60s. Well no, it could be early, in high school I was there in 1960. So yeah the repertoire we played out of the “Combo Ork” Books I think they were called. And the instrumentation worked on about — for about any number of players that you had. And then there were some — I can’t remember the publishers you know. But there wasn’t a lot of music for us to play. In fact by the time I got to college you know you had to, if you wanted to be competitive in these contests that we went to, or…

Yes. In those times it was AM radio played almost anything you could imagine, but what would the group have done if someone came up, put twenty bucks in the tip jar and said, © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
“Play some Sinatra”? And if you didn’t know any did you have the wherewithal that you could fake it?
